newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Foreign oil firms to take stake in Petrogal unit.
newsitem.headline: Foreign oil firms to take stake in Petrogal unit.

text.p: Four international oil companies will take stakes in a new subsidiary of Portuguese state oil company Petrogal, Petrogal officials said.

From the end of October the Royal Dutch/Shell group and Mobil Corp will each take a 15 percent stake in CLC-Companhia Logistica de Combustiveis SA while British Petroleum (BP) and Spain's Repsol will take five percent each, the officials told a news conference.
CLC, a storage and distribution unit wholly owned by Petrogal, expects to have share capital of between 8.0 and 10 billion escudos by the end of October.
CLC will operate a pipeline from Petrogal's Sines refinery in southwestern Portugal to a storage site in Aveiras 40 km (25 miles) north of Lisbon.
Petrogal officials said it would be the first European pipeline to carry both gas and liquid fuels.
Petrogal, which has been partially privatised, invested around 44 billion escudos in the project.
